newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on weather and fund selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on weather and fund selling.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a bearish weather forecast and on fund selling, traders said.
"It's fund selling, that's all it is," a trader said.

The fund sales totaled at least 20.0 million bushels with Rosenthal Collins a key seller of 11.0 million bushels of December, Griffin Trading sold eight million December and Refco Inc sold six million December and bought three million December, they said.
Corn Wednesday had closed firmer on some forecasts for wet weather and for frost this week in key U.S. corn states.

Traders said Wednesday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook for normal to above normal temperatures and normal to below normal precipitation in the U.S. Midwest from October 1 through October 5 hit the market, they said.
The lack of a killing frost this week also was cited.
Meteorologists early Thursday said rain would move across the Midwest Thursday and Friday, followed by cooler temperatures.
Corn futures closed 6-1/2 cents per bushel lower to 1-1/2 higher, with December down 6-1/4 at $3.06. March was down 6-1/2 at $3.12-1/2.
"We will be seeing cooler weather moving in after this front," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. "It's not the knockout freeze people were looking for."
Soybean and corn futures were supported Wednesday by some outlooks for frost late this week in the Midwest.
Technical traders cited sell stops hit when December broke below first support at $3.10-1/2 and stops again were hit when the next level, $3.08 was broken. The session low for December was $3.05-3/4.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 50,000 contracts, up from 37,668 Wednesday.

In corn options, Cargill Investor Services bought 1,000 December $3.50 calls at 7/8 to 1-1/4 cents, Rosenthal Collins sold 700 December $3.40 calls at 1-1/2 to 1-3/8 cents and Prudential Securities bought 800 December $2.80 puts at one cent.
Corn options volume was estimated at 24,000, down from Wednesday's total of 24,437.
